minutes.headline: Council on Aging sent a member's seven bylaw-change proposals to a four-member subcommittee and backed an architect study and emergency shower.
minutes.summary: The meeting covered a long member presentation proposing seven changes to the board's policies and procedures, which drew objections about its scope and its lack of advance notice and was sent to a subcommittee. The board also heard about the assessor's new office hours at the senior center after an elevator mishap at the Ritter building, and voted to pursue an architect study for a building expansion and a shower for emergency sheltering. Updates on the formula grant, parking lot, events, trips and the director's report rounded out the agenda.

votes.motion: Table the discussion of the seven policy-and-procedure changes and have the chair set a process, amended to appoint a subcommittee to collect recommendations and present them to the full board
Add to the budget request an architect to study a building expansion for additional resources for the senior center and town
Look at adding a shower to the bathroom so the senior center can serve as an emergency facility

budget_items.topic: State aging services funding and North Central Aging Services budget
budget_items.what_was_said: A member described the state aging services office budget and the regional agency's revenue, mostly from the state, with the rest from insurance and other payments.
The director gave the annual formula grant amount, a per-senior rate times the number of seniors. It rolls over, was partly spent on outside furniture, and is being used to subsidize trips.

budget_items.topic: Possible use of formula grant for architect study
budget_items.what_was_said: The director said the grant could possibly fund an architect study if it cost around the figure mentioned.

budget_items.topic: Parking lot design contract and construction
budget_items.what_was_said: The engineer's design contract was to be sent out, already funded from a previous capital plan. An estimator would then quote construction, with grants such as ADA grants to be sought.

budget_items.topic: One-off funding outside the capital plan, and playground fund
budget_items.what_was_said: The speaker cited the school turf field engineering request from free cash as an example of one-off funding outside the capital plan, and noted an existing fund for playground construction.

budget_items.topic: Subsidized trips funded by formula grant
budget_items.what_was_said: Two trips were funded with the formula grant: a theater trip priced below ticket price and a casino trip where the seat payment is refunded.
The board discussed whether to charge a fee for outside use of the facility and whether insurance would cover it; the question was left for follow-up with the select board.
Tickets for the evening Christmas party were given as a price per person.

budget_items.topic: Capital request for expansion and shower
budget_items.what_was_said: The expansion and shower would go through the capital request process to the facilities head, and could strengthen grant applications for the parking lot.

decisions.decision: A COA liaison to the ADA committee will be pursued after the chair confirms with the town manager; a member volunteered.
A subcommittee of four members (Chris, Jack, Anna, Susan) was formed; the presentation is to be sent to all members ahead of time.
The expansion and shower requests will go through the capital request process via the facilities head; the chair will talk to Pauline.
Council priorities for the FY28 budget will be on the next agenda.
Members volunteered to decorate trees for the Festival of Trees; the submission deadline was given as November 13th.
Two members will draft a COA board entry for the town report, pending a check with the town manager and town clerk.
The chair/director to find out who has authority over building usage and fees; the topic stays on the agenda.
The director will look into transportation for the evening Christmas party.
The assessor's new hours at the center are to be posted on the COA website via a PDF flyer.

what_happened.line: The Council on Aging voted to add an architect study of a building expansion to its budget request, and to look at adding a shower so the center can serve as an emergency facility.
A second voice vote supported looking at a shower in the bathroom so the senior center could serve as an emergency facility.
A member's presentation proposing seven changes to the board's policies and procedures was tabled, and a four-member subcommittee was formed to collect recommendations.
The expansion and shower requests will go through the capital request process via the facilities head, and the director said the formula grant could possibly fund the architect study.
The board heard that the assessor now holds office hours at the center, to be posted on the COA website, after an elevator mishap at the Ritter building.

why_it_matters: The expansion study and shower would go through the town's capital request process, so any cost would compete for capital funds and could end up before residents as a budget item.

The subcommittee's review of the board's policies and procedures will shape how the senior center's governing board is run, including term limits and adjunct members, before any change reaches a vote.
